newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish swine fever outbreak seen under control.
newsitem.headline: Spanish swine fever outbreak seen under control.

text.p: Spanish farmers in the Catalan province of Lerida believe the recent outbreak of swine fever is now under control after the regional government ordered pigs to be slaughtered and a transport ban.

"The measures were taken very quickly and after extending the ban zone, farmers beyond the area are confident that we've managed to stop it short," a spokesman for a regional farmers' association in Barcelona told Reuters on Friday.
Two areas in which the disease appeared had been identified, he said, and around 12,000 pigs have been sacrificed so far out of a total of about two million in the province.
On Thursday, the EU veterinary committee approved measures to establish an area in which pig transport is banned unless the animals are headed for slaughter in specially sealed lorries.
Counties affected by the transport ban are Pla D'Urgell, Urgell, Noguera, Segria and Garrigues.

In a statement, the Agriculture Ministry said the EU decision "confirms measures already put into practice and which ratify those adopted by the Catalan local government from the very moment when the disease was suspected."
The farmers' group spokesman said the swine fever had been found in pigs imported from the Netherlands.
"Farmers are still on the alert, but you could say that the immediate danger is over. The steps taken have been well-received by the community," he said.
A local grains trader said the number of pigs slaughtered was not sufficient to have any effect on feed prices.

"The number sacrificed so far has been minimal and the rest have had a transport ban imposed, so although they're not going anywhere, the animals are eating just the same," he said. -- Madrid newsroom +341 585 2160
